title: Accusative Case & Direct Objects
subtitle: Master the single biggest A1 shift: Masculine 'der → den' and 'ein → einen' for direct objects.

cheatSheet.summary: The Accusative case marks the direct object—the person or thing directly receiving the action of a verb (Who or what do you buy, see, have, or read?).
keyTakeaways: Good news: ONLY Masculine [M] changes in the Accusative! (der → den, ein → einen, mein → meinen).
Feminine [F] (die/eine), Neuter [N] (das/ein), and Plural [PL] (die) stay completely unchanged.
Always-Accusative prepositions (DOGFU): durch, ohne, gegen, für, um.
Common Accusative verbs: haben, kaufen, sehen, suchen, brauchen, trinken, essen, lesen, kennen.

patterns.translation: He is looking for the book.

cheatSheet.watchOut: After 'sein' (to be) and 'werden' (to become), NEVER use Accusative—always use Nominative ('Er ist ein guter Lehrer', NOT 'einen').

exercises.english: I see the dog in the park.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich sehe den Hund im Park.
exercises.rulePill: Verb 'sehen' takes an Accusative direct object → Masculine [M] 'der Hund' changes to 'den Hund'.

exercises.prompt: Wir brauchen ___ neuen Tisch für die Küche.
exercises.english: We need a new table for the kitchen.
exercises.fullGerman: Wir brauchen einen neuen Tisch für die Küche.
exercises.rulePill: 'brauchen' triggers Accusative → Masculine [M] 'ein Tisch' becomes 'einen Tisch'.

exercises.english: The gift is for my brother.
exercises.fullGerman: Das Geschenk ist für meinen Bruder.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'für' ALWAYS triggers Accusative → Masculine [M] 'mein Bruder' becomes 'meinen Bruder'.

exercises.prompt: Sie kauft ___ warmes Brot beim Bäcker.
exercises.english: She buys a warm loaf of bread at the bakery.
exercises.fullGerman: Sie kauft ein warmes Brot beim Bäcker.

nouns.caseTrigger: Direct object of 'kaufen' — Neuter [N] does NOT change in Accusative

exercises.rulePill: Only Masculine changes in Accusative! Neuter [N] 'das Brot' keeps 'ein' (never 'einen').

exercises.promptHint: Spot the Accusative preposition error and fix it.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'durch' ALWAYS triggers Accusative → Masculine [M] 'der Park' becomes 'den Park'.

exercises.prompt: Er geht niemals ohne ___ Schlüssel aus dem Haus.
exercises.english: He never leaves the house without the key.
exercises.fullGerman: Er geht niemals ohne den Schlüssel aus dem Haus.
exercises.rulePill: Preposition 'ohne' ALWAYS triggers Accusative → Masculine [M] 'der Schlüssel' becomes 'den Schlüssel'.

exercises.promptHint: Watch out for the Nominative trap after 'sein'!
exercises.rulePill: 'sein' links subject and identity—it NEVER takes Accusative! Use Nominative Masculine [M]: 'ein Arzt'.

exercises.instruction: Assemble the sentence with the Accusative direct object.
exercises.english: I drink a black coffee every morning.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich trinke jeden Morgen einen schwarzen Kaffee.
exercises.rulePill: Definite time expressions ('jeden Morgen') and direct objects ('einen schwarzen Kaffee') both take Accusative [M] '-en'.

exercises.subject: du
exercises.english: Do you have an appointment tonight?
exercises.fullGerman: Hast du heute Abend einen Termin?
exercises.rulePill: 'haben' drops the 'b' in du/er forms: du hast, er/sie/es hat (never 'habst').
